promise: Diagnose a broken agent session and prepare a reversible repair without inventing execution results.
audience: People repairing transcripts and provider/session integration.
trigger: A session cannot resume or provider errors suggest structural corruption.

modes.name: Diagnose
modes.when: A session or provider has failed.
modes.output: Severity-ranked findings with supported evidence and envelope limits.

modes.name: Repair
modes.output: A separate repaired copy and verification report.

modes.name: Escalate
modes.when: The format or failure remains uncertain.
modes.output: A minimal redacted support bundle and next diagnostic step.

examples.title: Recover an interrupted tool call
examples.brief: Use Session Doctor to inspect a disposable direct role/content JSONL transcript. Diagnose before changing anything. If a missing tool result is unambiguous, prepare a new repair copy that marks the result unavailable, preserve the original and explain the remaining host-resume check.
examples.before: An interrupted tool call is “fixed” by a fabricated successful result or truncated history.
examples.after: A new copy records the missing result as interrupted and leaves the original intact.
examples.why: The repaired structure remains honest about what actually executed.

boundaries: The helper supports direct role/content JSONL only; live resume and provider acceptance are separate checks.

verification.name: Functional acceptance
verification.expected: Supplied fictional tasks exercise actual mechanisms and failure boundaries.
verification.evidence: 326 retained native tests and 3 substantive direct-message repair checks passed; no live provider or session resume performed.

verification.name: Native host acceptance
verification.expected: Actual provider/host/desktop/daemon/runner acceptance for the selected adapter.
verification.evidence: No live model, real desktop transaction, invitation, deployment or production data migration was performed by this functional baseline.

sources.role: Primary retained owner history, mechanisms and records; portable method consolidates the listed entry points.

consolidation: One portable method entry with mode references; original native engines, agents and records retained as optional adapters.
publication_status: Installation and evidence scopes are documented below.

marketing.headline: Understand a broken session before you repair it.
marketing.lead: For people whose agent session will not resume. Session Doctor checks the supported transcript structure, names the ambiguity and prepares a separate repair copy when the evidence supports one, leaving the original available.

benefits.title: Keep the original intact
benefits.body: Diagnose first and write any supported repair to a new destination that cannot overwrite existing work.

benefits.title: See what is actually missing
benefits.body: Distinguish a missing tool result from malformed JSON, duplicate IDs or an unsupported event format.

benefits.title: Avoid invented history
benefits.body: A synthetic repair entry says interrupted with no result available; it never pretends an action completed.

walkthrough.title: Identify the format
walkthrough.detail: Record the host, transcript revision and failure class without exposing private transcript contents.

walkthrough.title: Inspect the structure
walkthrough.detail: Check supported direct role/content JSONL for pairing, duplicate IDs, malformed lines and advisory ordering concerns.

walkthrough.title: Prepare a copy and verify
walkthrough.detail: Repair only an unambiguous missing result into a new file, recheck it and separately test resumption in the actual host.

use_when: A supported direct-message JSONL transcript cannot resume.
A tool call appears to have no result after interruption.
You need a redacted diagnosis before host-specific recovery.
not_for: Blindly rewriting an unfamiliar event envelope.
Equating a structurally clean copy with provider acceptance.
marketing.quickstart_prompt: Use Session Doctor to inspect a disposable direct role/content JSONL transcript. Diagnose before changing anything. If a missing tool result is unambiguous, prepare a new repair copy that marks the result unavailable, preserve the original and explain the remaining host-resume check.
marketing.output_preview:
Diagnosis: one tool call has no result
Original: unchanged
Repair eligibility: only if pairing and order are otherwise unambiguous
New copy: explicit destination, must not already exist
Inserted status: interrupted; result unavailable

Still to check: actual host and provider accept the repaired copy.
marketing.example_note: Fictional diagnostic outline. No real session transcript was opened or modified for this example.
install_notes: Python 3.11 or later is required by the portable install/build helper. The installed method runs through your agent host.
The portable direct-message helper is Python stdlib-only and requires no provider key.
It reads at most the documented 16 MB limit; unsupported event envelopes are reported explicitly.
Optional failover, cache and host adapters have separate setup and acceptance requirements.
marketing.proof_summary: Native and functional fixtures cover supported structure, ambiguous failures and copy-only repair. They do not establish successful resumption in every host or provider.
marketing.next_step: Work on a disposable copy first and identify the exact transcript format before requesting a repair.
